ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p244/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p244/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p244/r9.claim: The people emerge visibly from their graves with no hill, building, or clothing to hide them; the earth is flat and they are raised barefoot and naked.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p244/r9.anchor: أي ظاهرون من قبورهم، لا يسترهم شيء من جبل أو أكمة أو بناء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p244/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p244/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p244/r10.claim: The phrase يوم هم بارزون is an apposition to يوم التلاق; Sibawayh rejects annexing a future time adverb to a nominal sentence, while Abu al-Hasan and some grammarians allow it, though rarely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p244/r10.anchor: ويوما بدل من يوم التلاق، وكلاهما ظرف مستقبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya makes يوم هم بارزون an inflected time adverb governed by لا يخفى, arguing that an adverb is built only when annexed to a non-declinable form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ويحتمل أن يكون انتصابه على الظرف، والعامل فيه قوله: لا يخفى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan says adverbs annexed to non-declinable forms need not always be built; inflection remains possible, and the treatment of يوم ينفع differs between Basrans and Kufans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r2.anchor: فالبناء ليس متحتما، بل يجوز فيه البناء والإعراب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r3.claim: For an adverb annexed to a nominal clause, the author prefers the Kufan allowance of either inflection or building because many examples support building.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r3.anchor: وهو الصحيح لكثرة شواهد البناء على ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r4.claim: A claim in some of the author's school that such an adverb must be built is mistaken; no grammarian held it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r4.anchor: وهذا قول لم يذهب إليه أحد، فهو وهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r5.claim: Nothing about the people is hidden from God, including their innermost thoughts and concealed states.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says that after all creatures perish, God asks who owns sovereignty, receives no answer, and answers himself: God, the One, the Subduer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إذا هلك من في السموات ومن في الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r7.claim: Ibn Masud describes all creatures gathered on a white plain like a silver ingot, where a caller asks who owns sovereignty and everyone answers God, the One, the Subduer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r7.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: يجمع الله الخلائق يوم القيامة في صعيد بأرض بيضاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r8.claim: Another report says God asks and the world falls silent from awe before he answers himself and people then answer; sovereignty is singled out on that day because it becomes evident to disbelievers and the ignorant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p245/r8.anchor: وإنما خص التقرير باليوم، وإن كان الملك له تعالى في ذلك اليوم وفي غيره

NAHHAS:v4p27/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p27/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p27/r13.claim: Hum barizūna is a subject and predicate; the whole clause is genitive after yawm, so its tanwīn is omitted. This works with a time understood as idh, not idhā.
NAHHAS:v4p27/r13.anchor: خبره والجملة في موضع خفض بالإضافة فلذلك حذفت التنوين من يوم وإنما يكون في هذا عند سيبويه إذا كان الظرف بمعنى إذ

NAHHAS:v4p27/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p27/r14.speaker: أبو وائل عن ابن مسعود
NAHHAS:v4p27/r14.claim: People are gathered on a white earth like silver, and a caller asks ‘To whom belongs sovereignty today?’ The author accepts this report and rejects the view that the question occurs with no creation present.
NAHHAS:v4p27/r14.anchor: أصح ما قيل فيه ما رواه أبو وائل عن ابن مسعود قال يحشر الناس على أرض بيضاء مثل الفضة لم يعص الله جل وعز عليها

NAHHAS:v4p27/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p27/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p27/r15.claim: All people answer that sovereignty belongs to God; believers say it joyfully, while unbelievers say it reluctantly in submission.
NAHHAS:v4p27/r15.anchor: فينادي مناد يوم القيامة ليقرر الناس لمن الملك اليوم فيقول العباد مؤمنهم وكافرهم لله الواحد القهار

STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.claim: Verses 10–20 warn of the disbelievers’ Hereafter; this sets up the extended Moses and Pharaoh account, centered on a believer in Pharaoh’s House challenging opposition to Moses.
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.anchor: Vv. 10–20 then tell of the place of the disbelievers in the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r3.claim: Verses 13–20 establish God’s control of mercy and calamity and exclusive right to worship and obedience; He alone masters Judgment Day, and idolaters have no intercessor.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r3.anchor: All mercies and calamities are in the control of God; hence only He is worthy of being worshipped and obeyed

ELMALILI:40:10-20/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:10-20/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:10-20/r22.claim: The Day of Meeting is Resurrection, when spirits and bodies, inhabitants of heaven and earth, deeds and doers, and worshipped beings and worshippers meet or clash.
ELMALILI:40:10-20/r22.anchor: “Telâkī Günü” kıyamet günüdür. Zira o gün rûhlar ve cisimler, göktekiler ve yerdekiler, ameller ve âmiller, mâbudlar ve âbidler telâkī edecekler

ELMALILI:40:10-20/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:10-20/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:10-20/r23.claim: On that day people emerge from their graves and stand exposed; nothing of themselves, their deeds, or their states is hidden from God.
ELMALILI:40:10-20/r23.anchor: o gün ki o halk hep burûz etmişler, kabirlerden[^17] çıkmış, açığa fırlamışlardır. Nefislerini örten, amellerini gizleyen hiçbir şey kalmamış

ELMALILI:40:10-20#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:10-20#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:10-20#2/r1.claim: Wahid means God cannot admit any partner or plurality in His essence; He has neither parts nor constituent units.
ELMALILI:40:10-20#2/r1.anchor: “Vâhid” zâtında hiç şirkete, kesrete ihtimâli yok; eczâsı da yok, cüz’iyyâtı da yok.

ELMALILI:40:10-20#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:10-20#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:10-20#2/r2.claim: Qahhar means everything is subject to God's overpowering; all perishes except His face, and He is sovereign to do what He wills.
ELMALILI:40:10-20#2/r2.anchor: “Kahhâr” bir şerîki olmak şöyle dursun her şey O’nun kahrına mahkum; كُلُّ شَىْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُۥ

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r1.claim: At the Gathering, all people reappear and none of their deeds is hidden from God; only God has absolute sovereignty and judges swiftly and justly, assigning each person Paradise or Hell without injustice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r1.anchor: bütün insanlar, –dünyadayken yaptıkları eylemlerin hiçbiri Allah’a gizli kalmaksızın– yeniden hayat sahnesine çıkacaklar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r2.claim: One interpretation has a caller ask who owns sovereignty that day and everyone gathered answer that it belongs to God alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r2.anchor: Bir yoruma göre bütün insanlar mahşerde toplandıklarında bir görevli, 16. âyetteki ifadesiyle “Bugün hükümranlık kimindir?” diye seslenecek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r3.claim: Another view identifies the questioner as one group of angels and the respondents as another group of angels.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r3.anchor: Soru soranın bir melekler topluluğu, cevap verenin de başka bir melekler topluluğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r4.claim: A further view says God Himself asks the question and gives the answer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r4.anchor: soru soranın ve cevap verenin bizzat yüce Allah olacağı yönünde görüşler de vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r5.claim: The verse powerfully depicts the fear, helplessness, and isolation people feel when they confront an afterlife they disbelieved in or neglected through heedlessness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:16/r5.anchor: âhiret gerçeğiyle yüz yüze gelince hissedecekleri korku ve çaresizliğin, içine düşecekleri yalnızlık halinin veciz ve sarsıcı bir ifadesi yer almaktadır.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p23/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p23/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p23/r1.claim: Every person's inner and outer self will be exposed before God, leaving no need for witnesses, evidence, excuses, lies, or false recommendations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p23/r1.anchor: The inner and outer self of every person will be exposed before God on that Day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p23/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p23/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p23/r2.claim: The question of who rules today challenges idolaters to say where the intercessors and deities they expected to save them have gone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p23/r2.anchor: Where are those intercessors and deities which these idolaters had set up as partners of God and thought that they would save them from God?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p23/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p23/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p23/r3.claim: God answers that sovereignty belongs to Him alone, the One and Almighty; no one can be another's friend or alter His decision.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p23/r3.anchor: no one will be able to be a friend to another nor be able to change a decision of God.

BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r1.claim: “Yawm hum bārizūn” is appositional to “the Day of Meeting”; baraza means to come out into open space or emerge into view after concealment.
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r1.anchor: بدل من يوم التلاق يقال : برز بروزا : خرج إلى البراز

BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r2.claim: People emerge from their graves or stand exposed without any mountain, hill, or building to hide them, because the earth is level that day.
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r2.anchor: خارجون من قبورهم ، أو ظاهرون لا يسترهم شيء من جبل

BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r3.claim: A cited hadith says people will be gathered barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised.
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r3.anchor: كما في الحديث : "يحشرون حفاة عراة غرلا

BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r4.claim: The source exempts believers who died away from home and had not fornicated: they will be clothed in garments from Paradise.
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r4.anchor: إلا قوما ماتوا في الغربة مؤمنين لم يزنوا ؛ فإنهم يحشرون

BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r5.speaker: رسول الله عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r5.claim: The Prophet says his community will be raised in its shrouds, while other communities are raised barefoot and naked.
BURSEVI:v8p125#3/r5.anchor: فإن أمتي يحشر بأكفانها وسائر الأمم حفاة عراة

BURSEVI:v8p126/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p126/r1.claim: Nothing of people or their deeds, whether manifest or hidden and whether past or future, is concealed from God; the author supports this with 69:18.
BURSEVI:v8p126/r1.anchor: ما من أعيانهم وأعمالهم الجلية والخفية السابقة واللاحقة مع كثرتهم كما قال تعالى :

BURSEVI:v8p126/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p126/r2.claim: In earthly life people imagined walls and screens could hide them and their deeds from God; that delusion disappears when they are exposed.
BURSEVI:v8p126/r2.anchor: وكانوا في الدنيا يتوهمون إنهم إذا استتروا بالحيطان والحجب فإن الله لا يراهم ويخفى عليه أعمالهم

BURSEVI:v8p126/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p126/r3.claim: One reading has a herald ask who owns the kingdom that day and answer the question himself: God, the One, the Overpowering.
BURSEVI:v8p126/r3.anchor: ينادي مناد لمن الملك اليوم ، فيجيب ؛ أي : ذلك المنادي بعينه

BURSEVI:v8p126/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p126/r4.claim: Alternatively, the entire assembly, believers and unbelievers, answers because even unbelievers gain necessary knowledge of divine oneness; they answer in regret, while believers rejoice in a truth they confessed in life.
BURSEVI:v8p126/r4.anchor: أو يجيبه أهل المحشر مؤمنهم وكافرهم لحصول العلم الضروري بالوحدانية

BURSEVI:v8p126/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p126/r5.claim: The question is a question of acknowledgment: the unbeliever answers in humiliation and regret, while the believer answers joyfully, having already said this in worldly life.
BURSEVI:v8p126/r5.anchor: لكن الكافر يقوله : صغارا ، وهو أنا وعلى سبيل التحسر والندامة

BURSEVI:v8p126/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p126/r6.claim: An alternative report names Idrīs as the one who answers.
BURSEVI:v8p126/r6.anchor: وقيل : إن المجيب إدريس عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v8p126/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p126/r7.claim: Although God owns everything at all times, the question singles out Judgment Day because worldly claims to kingship end then and no claimant remains.
BURSEVI:v8p126/r7.anchor: هو وإن كانفي جميع الأيام إلا أنه سبحانه ملك عباده في الدنيا

BURSEVI:v8p126/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126/r8.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p126/r8.claim: Kashf al-asrar depicts judgment as exposing hidden faults: the ungrateful rich face reckoning, the impatient poor are stripped of hypocrisy, and scholars without deeds and ostentatious reciters suffer public shame.
BURSEVI:v8p126/r8.anchor: دران روز رازها آشكار شود بردهاى متواريان درند توانكران بى شكررا در مقام حساب بدارند ودرويشان بى صبر را جامة نفاق از سر بركشند آتش فضيحت در طيلسان عالمان بى عمل زنند خاك ندامت بر فرق قراء مرائى ريزند

BURSEVI:v8p126/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126/r9.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p126/r9.claim: The same mystical description pictures some terrified people asking where the way to God is.

BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says only ignorance and lack of knowledge make people ask who owns the kingdom today: God has always been the true King, but people recognize this only when the afterlife compels them.
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : لولا سوء طبائع الجهالة وقلة معرفتهم لما ذكر الله قوله : لمن الملك اليوم

BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r2.claim: The One nullifies numerical multiplicity, while the Overpowering forces all to acknowledge incapacity and servitude, willingly or unwillingly.
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r2.anchor: والقهار : الذي قهر الكل على العجز بالإقرار له بالعبودية طوعا وكرها.

BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r3.claim: His shaykh sees an elegant order: divine oneness removes multiplicity and divine overpowering removes effects, so all vanishes and only God remains.
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r3.anchor: قال شيخي وسندي روح الله روحه في قوله : الواحد القهار ، ترتيب أنيق

BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r4.claim: Those who stand forth are annihilated from their own existence; nothing of that existence remains hidden as they are effaced until only God remains.
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r4.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يومهم بارزون ؛ أي : خارجون من وجودهم بالفناء لا يخفى على الله

BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r5.speaker: الجنيد
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r5.claim: The state is the station Junayd described as there being nothing in existence but God.
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r5.anchor: وهذا المقام الذي أشار إليه الجنيد قدس سره بقوله : ما في الوجود سوى الله

BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r6.claim: When nothing besides God owns existence, God alone is caller and respondent, answering “the One, the Overpowering” through His manifestation of the attribute of overpowering.
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r6.anchor: فإذا لم يكن لغير الله ملك الوجود يكون هو الداعي ، والمجيب ، فيقول : الواحد القهار

BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r7.speaker: جامى
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r7.claim: Jāmī says our beginning and return are unity alone, with multiplicity in between an illusion.
BURSEVI:v8p126#3/r7.anchor: جامى معاد ومبدأ ما وحدتست وبس ما درميانه كثرت موهوم والسلام

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180/r1.claim: Qatadah says people will be exposed with no mountain or other thing screening them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ يوم هم بارزون ﴾ قال بارزون لا يسترهم جبل ولا يسترهم شيء

QASHANI:40:16-18/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:40:16-18/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:40:16-18/r1.claim: On the day of appearing, people emerge from veils of selfhood or bodily coverings.
QASHANI:40:16-18/r1.anchor: عن حجاب الأنيات أو غواشي الأبدان

QASHANI:40:16-18/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:40:16-18/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:40:16-18/r2.claim: Nothing is hidden from God: concealed deeds become visible in their records and move from latency into appearance, as the cited verses say; alternatively, people emerge from veils of attributes into the Essence itself.
QASHANI:40:16-18/r2.anchor: لظهورها في صحائفهم وبروزها من الكمون إلى الظهور

QASHANI:40:16-18/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:40:16-18/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:40:16-18/r3.claim: When all are annihilated in the unity of the gathering, God asks who holds sovereignty; only He answers, the One beyond all else, the Subduer who annihilated all by His force.
QASHANI:40:16-18/r3.anchor: ينادي به الحق سبحانه عند فناء الكل في عين الجمع فيجيب هو وحده

QUSHAYRI:v3p132/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p132/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p132/r11.claim: God knows what exists and what is absent, past and future, what cannot occur, and how a possible event would unfold if it occurred.
QUSHAYRI:v3p132/r11.anchor: يعلم الحاصل الموجود ، ويعلم المعدوم المفقود ؛ والذي كان والذي يكون ، والذي لا يكون مما علم أنه لا يجوز أن يكون

QUSHAYRI:v3p132/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p132/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p132/r12.claim: God's dominion is never limited to a particular day or time; judgment day instead exposes human claims of ownership and their illusions as baseless.
QUSHAYRI:v3p132/r12.anchor: لا يتقيد ملكه بيوم ، ولا يختص ملكه بوقت ، ولكن دعاوى الخلق - اليوم - لا أصل لها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r1.claim: “The Day they emerge” replaces “the Day of the Meeting”; under Abū al-Ḥasan, the nominal clause is genitive in the temporal phrase, while Sībawayh requires an implied verb after the adverb.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r1.anchor: ( يوم هم بارزون ( بدل من ( يوم التلاق ) و ( هم ) مبتدأ و ( بارزون ) خبر والجملة في محل جر بإضافة ( يوم ) إليها قيل : وهذا تخريج على مذهب أبي الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r2.claim: Another grammatical analysis makes the day an adverb modifying “nothing is hidden from God”; the author regards the replacement analysis as the apparent one.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r2.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ( يوم ) ظرفا لقوله تعالى : ( لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء ( والظاهر البدلية

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r3.claim: The sentence may resume the description to explain their exposure and remove the false worldly assumption that they could remain concealed; another option makes it a second predicate or a circumstantial clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r3.anchor: وهذه الجملة استئناف لبيان بروزهم وتقرير له وإزاحة لما كان يتوهمه بعض المتوهمين في الدنيا من الاستتار توهما باطلا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Day of the Meeting is named for the gathering of all creatures.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لالتقاء الخلائق فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r5.claim: Muqātil says it is the day when Creator and created meet; some scholars prefer this interpretation because it matches other uses of meeting the Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل : لالتقاء الخالق والمخلوق فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r6.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says the name refers to the meeting of the people of Heaven and the people of Earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r6.anchor: وقال السدي : لالتقاء أهل السماء وأهل الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r7.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r7.claim: Maymūn ibn Mihrān says it is when the oppressor and oppressed meet.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r7.anchor: وقال ميمون بن مهران : لالتقاء الظالم والمظلوم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r8.speaker: الثعلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r8.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits the view that it is the meeting of every person with their deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r8.anchor: وحكى الثعلبي أن ذلك لالتقاء كل امريء وعمله

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r9.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r9.claim: The author of al-Kashf prefers Ibn ʿAbbās's first view because it follows the literal sense and makes each phrase independently awe-inspiring: all creatures gather, then appear before their sovereign.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r9.anchor: وقال صاحب الكشف : القول الأول وهو ما نقل عن ابن عباس أولا أشبه لجريان الكلام فيه على الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r10.claim: Barūz means becoming visible in an open plain; here nothing shields them, since the Earth will be level and empty of hills, mounds, or buildings.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r10.anchor: وأصله حصل في براز أي قضاء والمراد ظاهرون لا يسترهم شيء من جبل أو أكمة أو بناء لأن الأرض يومئذ قاع صفصف

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r11.speaker: النبي ﷺ
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet's description of people meeting God barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r11.anchor: كما جاء في الصحيحين عن ابن عباس سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : إنكم ملاقو الله حفاة عراة غرلا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r12.claim: Other explanations say the people emerge from their graves or that their deeds and inner secrets become manifest.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r12.anchor: وقيل : المراد خارجون من قبورهم أو ظاهرة أعمالهم وسرائرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r13.claim: A further explanation says their souls are exposed without the veils of bodies, but the author says this lacks support from an infallible authority.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r13.anchor: وقيل : ظاهرة نفوسهم لا تحجب بغواشي الأبدان مع تعلقها بها ولا يقبل هذا بدون ثبت من المعصوم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r14.claim: “From them” may mean their states and deeds or their persons; the author chooses the inclusive reading: nothing about their persons, actions, or conditions, overt, hidden, past, or future, escapes God.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p56#2/r14.anchor: والمراد بقوله تعالى : ( منهم ) على ما قيل : من أحوالهم وأعمالهم وقيل : من أعيانهم واختير التعميم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p57/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p57/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p57/r5.claim: The question about sovereignty and its answer are narrated as speech, either attached to the preceding negative sentence or introduced as a reply to the question raised by their appearing.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p57/r5.anchor: حكاية لما يسئل عنه في ذلك اليوم ولما يجاب به بتقدير قول معطوف على ما قبله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p143#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p143#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p143#3/r1.claim: On that day people emerge visibly from their graves with nothing concealing them; God knows all their deeds and circumstances.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p143#3/r1.anchor: يوم هم بارزون} خارجون من قبورهم ظاهرون لا يسترهم شيء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p143#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p143#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p143#3/r2.claim: After all creation has perished, God asks who holds dominion today; no one answers, so He answers Himself: it belongs to God, the One who subdues creation through death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p143#3/r2.anchor: يقول الله تعالى في ذلك اليوم بعد فناء الخلق: {لمن الملك اليوم} فلا أحد يجيبه

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:16-17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:16-17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:16-17/r1.claim: On the Day people are exposed, they have left their graves, or are visible without cover, or their souls, deeds, and secrets are made manifest.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:16-17/r1.anchor: خارجون من قبورهم أو ظاهرون لا يسترهم شيء أو ظاهرة نفوسهم لا تحجبهم غواشي الأبدان، أو أعمالهم وسرائرهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:16-17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:16-17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:16-17/r2.claim: Nothing about their persons, deeds, or states is hidden from God; this confirms their exposure and removes worldly assumptions.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:16-17/r2.anchor: من أعيانهم وأعمالهم وأحوالهم، وهو تقرير لقوله { هم برزون } وإزاحة لنحو ما يتوهم في الدنيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:16-17/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:16-17/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:16-17/r3.claim: ‘Whose is the kingdom today?’ narrates the question and answer, or states what the manifest disappearance of causes and intermediaries indicates; in reality it always testifies to God’s sole dominion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:16-17/r3.anchor: حكاية لما يسأل عنه في ذلك اليوم ولما يجاب به، أو لما دل عليه ظاهر الحال فيه من زوال الأسباب وارتفاع الوسائط، وأما حقيقة الحال فناطقة بذلك دائما

SULAMI:v2p208#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p208#3/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p208#3/r1.claim: Nothing can be concealed from God: He discloses what people hide, so they cannot hide anything from Him.
SULAMI:v2p208#3/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي - رحمة الله عليه - : كيف تخفى عليه وهو الذي يبديها عليهم وكيف يستترون عنه بشيء

SULAMI:v2p208#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p208#3/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p208#3/r2.claim: Jaʿfar says God silences all animate creatures when He asks who owns dominion, then answers for Himself because no one else can rightly answer.
SULAMI:v2p208#3/r2.anchor: قال جعفر : أخرس المكونات ذوات الأرواح عن جواب سؤاله في قوله لمن الملك اليوم

SULAMI:v2p208#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p208#3/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p208#3/r3.claim: Those who survey their deeds and worship receive recompense without injustice; those who behold God's grace rise beyond recompense to generosity and mercy.
SULAMI:v2p208#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : من طالع من نفسه أفعاله وأذكاره وطاعاته جزى على ذلك ولا ظلم عليه فيه

SULAMI:v2p208#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p208#3/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p208#3/r4.claim: God shows people the recompense due for their deeds so that they may then recognize the greater place of grace and generosity.
SULAMI:v2p208#3/r4.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر : يريك جزاء كسبك وما تستحق ذلك لترى بعد ذلك محل الفضل والكرم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r1.claim: On Resurrection, people are exposed outwardly and inwardly, with no cover at all.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r1.anchor: { يوم هم } أي بظواهرهم وبواطنهم { بارزون } أي برزوا لا ساتر فيه أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r2.claim: Nothing about anyone, outward or inward and whether exposed or hidden, escapes God's knowledge and power on that day or any other.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r2.anchor: أي المحيط علما وقدرة { منهم شيء } أي من ذواتهم ولا معانيهم سواء ظهروا أو استتروا في هذا اليوم وفي غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r3.claim: The question of who owns the kingdom dramatizes a victorious king confronting rebels brought before him; the defeated answer by speech or by their state.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r3.anchor: أن الملك العظيم إذا أرسل جيشه إلى من طال تمردهم عليه وعنادهم له فظفروا بهم وأحضروهم إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r4.speaker: بعض من قال
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r4.claim: An unnamed poet pictures long silence ending in a cry that makes the rebels weep blood, illustrating the forced answer to the divine question.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r4.anchor: سكت الدهر طويلا عنهم قد أبكاهم دما حين نطق

BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r5.claim: God alone owns every perfection; al-Wāḥid means He has no second through partnership, division, or any other form of sharing.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r5.anchor: الذي له جميع صفات الكمال , ثم دل على ذلك بقوله : { الواحد } أي الذي لا يمكن أن يكون له ثان بشركة ولا قسمة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r6.claim: Al-Qahhār means God continually subdues whomever He wills; this follows from absolute self-sufficiency grounded in true oneness.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p494#2/r6.anchor: { القهار * } أي الذي يقهر من يشاء متكررا وصفه بذلك دائما أبدا لما ثبت من غناه المطلق بوحدانيته الحقيقة

DURR-FULL:v7p278/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p278/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p278/r3.claim: On the day people stand exposed, no mountain or anything else will shield them.
DURR-FULL:v7p278/r3.anchor: {يوم هم بارزون} ولا يسترهم جبل ولا شيء

DURR-FULL:v7p278/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p278/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p278/r5.claim: Nothing is hidden from God even now; on the Resurrection Day people will stand exposed, unable to hide behind mountains or dwellings.
DURR-FULL:v7p278/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {يوم هم بارزون لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء} قال: واليوم لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء ولكنهم برزوا لله يوم القيامة لا يستترون بجبل ولا مدر

DURR-FULL:v7p278/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p278/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p278/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that before the Hour a herald will announce it to the living and dead; God descends to the lowest heaven and declares that sovereignty belongs to Him, the One, the Irresistible. Al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v7p278/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: ينادي مناد بين يدي الساعة: يا أيها الناس أتتكم الساعة فيسمعها الأحياء والأموات

DURR-FULL:v7p278/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p278/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p278/r7.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that between the blasts a herald announces the Hour in a voice heard by living and dead; God descends to the lowest heaven, then the proclamation names Him the One, the Irresistible.
DURR-FULL:v7p278/r7.anchor: عن أبي سعيد رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ينادي مناد بين الصيحة: يا أيها الناس أتتكم الساعة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3265/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3265/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3265/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that a caller announces the Hour to the living and dead, then God descends to the lowest heaven and declares that dominion belongs to Him alone.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3265/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : ينادي مناد بين يدي الساعة : يا ايها الناس ، اتتكم الساعة فيسمعها الاحياء والاموات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r1.claim: The muṣḥaf writes al-talāqī without yāʾ; Nāfiʿ and a transmission from Abū ʿAmr read it with kasra and no yāʾ, while the other readers retain yāʾ in connected speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r1.anchor: وكتب { التلاقي } في المصحف بدون ياء . وقرأه نافع وأبو عمرو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r2.claim: Since the word occurs in connected speech, dropping its yāʾ lacks a reason except treating connection as pause, rare in prose; the transmissions of Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr suffice as attestation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r2.anchor: لأنه وقع في الوصل لا في الوقف فلا موجب لطرح الياء إلا معاملة الوصل معاملة الوقف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r3.claim: Yawm hum bārizūn is an apposition to Yawm al-talāqī; it is a nominal clause in a future time adverb without ellipsis, the stronger analysis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r3.anchor: و { يوم هم بارزون } بدل من { يوم التلاقي } . و { هم بارزون } جملة اسمية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r4.claim: The third-person pronoun refers back to the disbelievers mentioned in 40:14.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r4.anchor: وضمير الغيبة عائد إلى { الكافرون من قوله : ولو كره الكافرون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r5.claim: The statement that nothing is hidden from Allah explains their appearing: their outward and inward states are wholly manifest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r5.anchor: وجملة { لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء } بيان لجملة { هم بارزون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r6.claim: The explicit name Allah is clearer because its antecedent is remote in the ensuing phrase about whom He wills among His servants; the subject of warn most likely refers to that relative pronoun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r6.anchor: وإظهار اسم الجلالة لأن إظهاره أصرح لبعد معاده بما عقبه من قوله : { على من يشاء من عباده }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r7.claim: Minhum means the whole group and their circumstances; the plural pronoun permits an understood modifier suited to context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r7.anchor: ومعنى { منهم } من مجموعهم ، أي من مجموع أحوالهم وشؤونهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r8.claim: The word shayʾ is maximally general, so nothing in their outward or inward states is hidden; the wording is broader than saying no person is hidden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r8.anchor: وأوثر أيضا لفظ { شيء } لتوغله في العموم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r9.claim: The question and answer are introduced through an omitted verb of saying: Allah is understood to say, Who owns sovereignty today, either as a circumstantial clause or a rhetorical restart.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r9.anchor: مقول لقول محذوف ، وحذف القول من حديث البحر . والتقدير : يقول الله لمن الملك اليوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r10.claim: The question may make tyrants acknowledge that their earthly claims of power for idols or themselves were false, exemplified by pagan deities, Pharaoh, and royal titles.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r10.anchor: والاستفهام إما تقريري ليشهد الطغاة من أهل المحشر على أنفسهم أنهم كانوا في الدنيا مخطئين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r11.claim: The question also rebukes idolaters who assigned different gods to particular peoples and domains, including the Greeks, Egyptians, and Arab tribes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r11.anchor: مثل قول اليونان بإلاه البحر وإلاه الحرب وإلاه الحكمة ، وقول أقباط مصر بإلاه الشمس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r12.claim: A report about the Resurrection has God say, I am the King; where are the kings of earth? Ibn ʿĀshūr reads this as frightening earthly rulers by asking where their grandeur has gone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p109/r12.anchor: ثم يقول الله أنا الملك أين ملوك الأرض ) استفهاما مرادا منه تخويفهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r1.claim: The question may build anticipation for its answer, so the answer settles more deeply in the listener; the question to the Prophet’s servants in 2:186 is a parallel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r1.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يكون الاستفهام كناية عن التشويق إلى ما يرد بعده من الجواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r2.claim: Al-yawm means the present day relative to the time when the reported statement is uttered.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r2.anchor: و { اليوم } المعرف باللام هو اليوم الحاضر ، وحضوره بالنسبة إلى القول المحكي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r3.claim: The declaration that sovereignty belongs to Allah alone may be the rest of the same divine utterance, with the speaker answering His own rhetorical question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r3.anchor: يجوز أن تكون من بقية القول المقدر الصادر من جانب الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r4.claim: Alternatively, a separate omitted speech has the people present answer that sovereignty belongs to Allah the One, the Subduer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r4.anchor: أي فيقول المسؤولون : { لله الواحد القهار } إقرارا منهم بذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r5.claim: The names One and Subduer suit the question of sovereignty because the scene displays Allah’s unity and His domination of tyrants and despots.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r5.anchor: وذكر الصفتين { الواحد القهار } دون غيرهما من الصفات العلى لأن لمعنييهما مزيد مناسبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r6.claim: The three following clauses remain connected to the divine utterance, whether the previous answer is one speech or an answer by the gathered people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p110/r6.anchor: لا ريب في أن هذه الجمل الثلاث متصلة بالمقول الصادر من جانب الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r11.claim: People stand on an exposed plain where sight reaches them and the caller can be heard.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r11.anchor: معناه في براز من الأرض ينفذهم البصر ويسمعهم الداعي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r12.claim: “Day” is accusative as an appositive to the earlier day, or possibly as an adverb governed by “nothing is hidden”; it is declined, not indeclinable, as the grammar and cited poetry show.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r12.anchor: ونصب يوم على البدل من الأول فهو نصب المفعول، ويحتمل أن ينصب على الظرف ويكون العامل فيه قوله: لا يخفى وهي حركة إعراب لا حركة بناء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r13.speaker: النابغة الذبياني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r13.claim: Al-Nabigha's verse supplies an example of the inflected temporal expression “when.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r13.anchor: وكقول الشاعر [النابغة الذبياني] : [الطويل] على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصبا ... وقلت ألما أصح والشيب وارع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r14.claim: Nothing about people is hidden from God, including their inner states, secrets, and thoughts held in their breasts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r14.anchor: وقوله تعالى: لا يخفى على الله منهم أي من بواطنهم وسرائرهم ودعوات صدورهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r15.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r15.claim: Ubayy's codex adds “upon Him” and reads that nothing is hidden from Him concerning them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p550#3/r15.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي بن كعب: «لا يخفى عليه منهم شيء» بضمير بدل المكتوبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r1.claim: One report says God asks who owns the kingdom that day, creation falls silent in awe, and God answers: “God, the One, the Overpowering.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r1.anchor: روي أن الله تعالى يقرر هذا التقرير ويسكت العالم هيبة وجزعا، فيجيب هو نفسه بقوله: لله الواحد القهار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r2.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r2.claim: Hasan al-Basri says God Himself is both the questioner and the respondent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r2.anchor: قال الحسن بن أبي الحسن هو تعالى السائل وهو المجيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says God asks the question and the assembled people answer it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r3.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: أنه تعالى يقرر فيجيب العالم بذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r4.claim: Another view says an angel calls out the question and the people answer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r4.anchor: وقيل ينادي بالتقرير ملك فيجيب الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r5.claim: A believer recognizes that no creature has independent power: sovereignty belongs to God throughout time, though its visibility to unbelievers and the ignorant becomes unmistakable at Judgment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p551/r5.anchor: وإذا تأمل المؤمن أنه لا حول لمخلوق ولا قوة إلا بالله، فالزمان كله وأيام الدهر أجمع إنما الملك فيها لله الواحد القهار، لكن ظهور ذلك للكفرة والجهلة يتضح يوم القيامة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r1.claim: On that day people are exposed, meaning they emerge visibly from their graves; nothing about them is hidden from God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ يوم هم بارزون ﴾ أي ظاهرون من قبورهم ﴿ لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r2.claim: Although nothing is hidden from God now, the wording serves as a threat of recompense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r2.anchor: فالجواب أن لا غير أن معنى الكلام التهديد بالجزاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r3.claim: One explanation is that none of their deeds is hidden from God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r3.anchor: أحدها لا يخفى عليه مما عملوا شيء قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r4.claim: Another explanation is that they cannot shelter from God behind a mountain or a structure of mud.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r4.anchor: والثاني لا يستترون منه بجبل ولا مدر قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r5.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r5.claim: A third explanation is that God brings them all out, since none of them is hidden from Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r5.anchor: والثالث أن المعنى أبرزهم جميعا لأنه لا يخفى عليه منهم شيء حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r6.claim: All agree that God asks 'To whom belongs sovereignty today?' after all creatures have perished, but they differ on when He says it: either at their extinction, when no one remains to answer and God answers Himself, or on the Day of Resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r6.anchor: اتفقوا على أن هذا يقوله الله عز وجل بعد فناء الخلائق واختلفوا في وقت قوله له على قولين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r7.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r7.claim: One view is that God answers Himself after the creatures fall silent.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r7.anchor: أحدهما أنه يجيب نفسه وقد سكت الخلائق لقوله قاله عطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r8.claim: Another view is that all creatures answer Him: 'To God, the One, the Irresistible.'
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p211#2/r8.anchor: فيقولون ﴿ لله الواحد القهار ﴾ قاله ابن جريج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r1.claim: All people will stand exposed, with nothing to shelter, shade, or conceal them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r1.anchor: أي: ظاهرون بادون كلهم، لا شيء يكنهم ولا يظلهم ولا يسترهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r2.claim: Nothing is hidden from God because everyone is equally present within His knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r2.anchor: أي: الجميع في علمه على السواء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r3.claim: A previously cited report says God folds the heavens and earth in His hand, declares Himself King, Mighty, and Proud, then asks where earthly kings and tyrants are.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r3.anchor: قد تقدم في حديث ابن عمر: أنه تعالى (2) يطوي السموات والأرض بيده، ثم يقول: أنا الملك، أنا الجبار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r4.claim: In the Trumpet report, after taking every creature's soul and remaining alone, God asks three times who owns sovereignty and answers that it belongs to Him, the One who overcomes everything.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r4.anchor: إذا قبض أرواح جميع خلقه، فلم يبق سواه وحده لا شريك له، حينئذ يقول: لمن الملك اليوم؟ ثلاث مرات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports a caller before the Hour announcing its arrival to the living and dead; God descends to the lowest heaven and recites the verse's question and answer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p136/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس [رضي الله عنهما] (5) قال: ينادي مناد بين يدي الساعة: يا أيها الناس، أتتكم الساعة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p160#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p160#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p160#2/r10.claim: On the day people emerge, nothing—a mountain, hill, or building—conceals them, since the earth is exposed and level; they are naked and uncovered.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p160#2/r10.anchor: ظاهرون لا يسترهم شيء من جبل أو أكمة أو بناء ، لأن الأرض بارزة قاع صفصف ، ولا عليهم ثياب ، إنما هم عراة مكشوفون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r1.claim: A hadith says people will be gathered naked, barefoot, and uncircumcised.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r2.claim: ‘Nothing is hidden from God’ means none of their deeds or conditions is hidden.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r2.anchor: { لا يخفى على الله منهم شىء } . أي : أن أعمالهم وأحوالهم .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿud states that nothing about them is hidden from God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r3.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : لا يخفى عليه منهم شيء .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r4.claim: The statement explains their exposure by correcting their worldly assumption that walls and screens could hide them or their deeds from God; their emergence leaves no room for that delusion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r4.anchor: كانوا يتوهمون في الدنيا إذا استتروا بالحيطان والحجب : أن الله لا يراهم ويخفى عليه أعمالهم ، فهم اليوم صائرون من البروز والانكشاف إلى حال لا يتوهمون فيها مثل ما كانوا يتوهمونه .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r5.claim: The verse is linked to the statement that people assumed God did not know much of what they did, to 4:108's distinction between hiding from people and God, and to 14:48's appearance before the One, the Irresistible.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r5.anchor: قال الله تعالى : ولكن ظننتم أن الله لا يعلم كثيرا مما تعملون . وقال تعالى : { يستخفون من الناس ولا يستخفون من الله } ( النساء : 108 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r6.claim: ‘Whose is the kingdom today?’ is staged as a herald's question answered by the people gathered for judgment: ‘God's, the One, the Irresistible.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r6.anchor: حكاية لما يسئل عنه في ذلك اليوم ولما يجاب به . ومعناه : أنه ينادي مناد فيقول : لمن الملك اليوم ؟ فيجيبه أهل المحشر : لله الواحد القهار .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r7.claim: Another account says all creatures gather on a white plain like a silver ingot where no one ever disobeyed God, and the first utterance is the herald's question and answer, followed by the declaration that each soul is recompensed; this account makes the herald both caller and respondent.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p161/r7.anchor: وقيل : يجمع الله الخلائق يوم القيامة في صعيد واحد بأرض بيضاء كأنها سبيكة فضة لم يعص الله فيها قط

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r17.claim: The people stand exposed as they emerge from their graves.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r17.anchor: { يوم هم بارزون } يعني من قبورهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r18.claim: One interpretation says God brings them all forth because nothing about them is hidden from Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r18.anchor: أحدهما : أنه أبرزهم جميعا لأنه لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r19.claim: Alternatively, He repays them, knowing every one of their deeds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r19.anchor: الثاني : معناه يجازيهم من لا يخفى عليه من أعمالهم شيء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r20.speaker: محمد بن كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r20.claim: One account places God's question about dominion between the two trumpet blasts, when creatures are dead and only the Creator remains; He answers Himself that dominion belongs to the One who remains alone and overpowers creation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r20.anchor: فيجيب نفسه فيقول : { لله الواحد القهار } لأنه بقي وحده وقهر خلقه , قاله محمد بن كعب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r21.claim: Another account places the question on Resurrection Day, when no one remains to claim ownership or a partner.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r21.anchor: الثاني : أن هذا من قول الله تعالى في القيامة حين لم يبق من يدعي ملكا , أو يجعل له شريكا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r22.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r22.claim: Ata says God answers Himself because the creatures are silent.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r22.anchor: فيقول : لله الواحد القهار ، قاله عطاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r23.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r23.claim: Ibn Jurayj says all creatures, believers and unbelievers, answer that dominion belongs to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p147/r23.anchor: فيقولون : لله الواحد القهار ، قاله ابن جريج

MUQATIL:40:16-18/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:40:16-18/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:40:16-18/r1.claim: People emerge from their graves onto the earth, spread like a stretched hide, and none is hidden from God.
MUQATIL:40:16-18/r1.anchor: ثم ذكر ذلك اليوم، فقال: { يوم هم بارزون } من قبورهم على ظهر الأرض مثم الأديم الممدود { لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء }

MUQATIL:40:16-18/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:40:16-18/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:40:16-18/r2.claim: After taking the heavens and earth in His right hand, God asks who owns sovereignty; no one answers, so He answers that it belongs to God alone, without partner, who overpowers creatures when resurrecting them.
MUQATIL:40:16-18/r2.anchor: حين قبض السموات والأرض فى يده اليمنى فلا يجيبه أحد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r1.claim: The resurrected stand exposed, with no mountain, hill, or building screening them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r1.anchor: ظاهرون لا يسترهم شىء من جبل أو اكمة أو بناء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r2.claim: Nothing about their deeds or circumstances is hidden from God.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r2.anchor: ﴿ لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء ﴾ اى من اعمالهم واحوالهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r3.claim: God asks who owns sovereignty that day, then answers Himself; the sole sovereign has subdued creation through death.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r3.anchor: اى يقول الله تعالى ذلك حين لا أحد يجيبه ثم يجيب نفسه بقوله ﴿ لله الواحد القهار ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r4.claim: An alternative has a caller ask who owns sovereignty, with the people gathered answering that it belongs to God, the One, the Subduer.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p69#5/r4.anchor: وقيل ينادى مناد فيقول لمن الملك اليوم فيجيبه اهل المحشر لله الواحد القهار

QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r4.claim: The clause about people being exposed may be an apposition to the first “day”; alternatively it is a nominal sentence genitive to “day,” a construction Sibawayh permits when the time word means “when.”
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r4.anchor: يكون بدلا من يوم الأول. وقيل: «هم» في موضع رفع بالابتداء و«بارزون» خبره والجملة في موضع خفض بالإضافة

QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r5.claim: The exposed are those emerging from their graves with nothing concealing them, as the earth is level and featureless, as explained under Taha.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r5.anchor: ومعنى: «بارزون» خارجون من قبورهم لا يسترهم شيء لأن الأرض يومئذ قاع صفصف لا عوج فيها ولا أمتا

QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r6.claim: The clause “nothing is hidden from God” can govern the time phrase “when they are exposed,” covering people and their deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r6.anchor: قيل: إن هذا هو العامل في «يوم هم بارزون» أي لا يخفى عليه شيء منهم ومن أعمالهم

QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r7.claim: The question about sovereignty occurs when creation has perished; al-Hasan says God asks and answers Himself because no one else answers.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r7.anchor: وذلك عند فناء الخلق. وقال الحسن: هو السائل تعالى وهو المجيب لأنه يقول ذلك حين لا أحد يجبيه

QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r8.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r8.claim: Al-Nahhas calls the report from Ibn Masʿud the soundest account: all people answer the herald on a white plain, believers gladly and unbelievers in grief and submission.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r8.anchor: وأصح ما قيل فيه ما رواه أبو وائل عن ابن مسعود قال: يحشر الناس على أرض بيضاء مثل الفضة

QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r9.claim: The author favors the first interpretation: God's solitary sovereignty is displayed after every claimant, kingdom, and lineage has vanished.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r9.anchor: قلت: والقول الأول ظاهر جدا لأن المقصود إظهار انفراده تعالى بالملك عند انقطاع دعاوى المدعين وانتساب المنتسبين

QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r10.claim: The author supports this display of sovereignty with the report that God declares Himself King when taking the earth and souls and folding the heavens.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:15-16/r10.anchor: ودل على هذا قوله الحق عند قبض الأرض والأرواح وطي السماء:

QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r1.claim: A report says God folds the earth in His left hand and the heavens in His right, then asks where the tyrants and arrogant have gone.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r1.anchor: وفي حديث ابن عمر: ثم يطوي الأرض بشماله والسموات بيمينه، ثم يقول: أنا الملك أين الجبارون أين المتكبرون.

QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r2.claim: Ibn Umar explains the sovereignty question as the end of worldly time, followed by resurrection and gathering.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r2.anchor: وعنه قوله سبحانه: { لمن الملك اليوم } هو انقطاع زمن الدنيا وبعده يكون البعث والنشر.

QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r3.claim: Between the two trumpet blasts, creation has died while the Creator remains; He asks and answers Himself as the sole owner who has subdued creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r3.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب قوله سبحانه: { لمن الملك اليوم } يكون بين النفختين حين فني الخلائق وبقي الخالق

QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r4.claim: Another report says a herald asks who owns sovereignty and the people of Paradise answer “God, the One, the All-Subduer”; al-Qurtubi leaves the matter to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:16-17/r4.anchor: وقيل: إنه ينادي مناد فيقول: «لمن الملك اليوم» فيجيبه أهل الجنة: { لله الواحد القهار } فالله أعلم.

RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r1.claim: The commentators say God asks and answers whose is the kingdom after all inhabitants of the heavens and earth have perished; Rāzī rejects this as a weak view.
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون إذا هلك كل من السموات ومن في الأرض فيقول الرب تعالى : { لمن الملك اليوم }

RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r2.claim: The call occurs on the Day of Meeting, when people are alive and appear before God to receive recompense, so it cannot occur only after all creation has perished.
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى بين أن هذا النداء إنما يحصل يوم التلاق ويوم البروز ويوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت ، والناس في ذلك الوقت أحياء

RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r3.claim: Speech must serve a purpose, but divine speech cannot be explained as self-reminding for memory, taking pleasure in one’s own words, or worship through remembrance; this further undermines the first view.
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r3.anchor: فثبت أن قول من يقول إن الله تعالى يذكر هذا النداء حال هلاك جميع المخلوقات باطل لا أصل له

RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r4.claim: The alternative view places the call among the gathered first and last: a herald asks whose is the kingdom and all present answer that it belongs to God, the One, the Overwhelming.
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r4.anchor: نادى مناد { لمن الملك اليوم } فيقول كل الحاضرين في محفل القيامة { لله الواحد القهار }

RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r5.claim: On the gathering view, believers answer with delight at their honored remembrance, while unbelievers answer in abasement and regret for having missed this confession in worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r5.anchor: فالمؤمنون يقولون تلذذا بهذا الكلام ، حيث نالوا بهذا الذكر المنزلة الرفيعة ، والكفار يقولونه على الصغار والذلة

RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r6.claim: Even if the first view is soundly transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās and others, it could mean that the call follows human extinction while angels remain to hear it.
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r6.anchor: إن صح القول الأول عن ابن عباس وغيره لم يمتنع أن يكون المراد أن هذا النداء يذكر بعد فناء البشر إلا أنه حضر هناك ملائكة يسمعون ذلك النداء

RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r7.claim: Rāzī says the caller and respondent could both be God, or different groups of angels; all these possibilities are open and no proof identifies one.
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r7.anchor: لا يبعد أيضا أن يكون السائل جمعا من الملائكة والمجيب جمعا آخرين ، الكل ممكن وليس على التعيين دليل

RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r8.claim: Rāzī ends this discussion by asking why the proclamation is particular to this day; this excerpt does not give the answer.
RAZI-FULL:v27p41/r8.anchor: فإن قيل وما الفائدة في تخصيص هذا اليوم بهذا النداء ؟

STUDYQURAN:40:16/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:16/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:16/r1.claim: On the Day of Resurrection, all humanity comes from its graves and gathers on one plain.
STUDYQURAN:40:16/r1.anchor: When all human beings come forth from their graves and are gathered on a single plain

STUDYQURAN:40:16/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:16/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:40:16/r2.claim: One reported interpretation has all those gathered answer that sovereignty belongs to God, the One, the Paramount.
STUDYQURAN:40:16/r2.anchor: all who are gathered will respond, It is God’s, the One, the Paramount (Q, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:40:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:16/r3.speaker: IK, Q, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:40:16/r3.claim: Another interpretation has God Himself answer the question about sovereignty.
STUDYQURAN:40:16/r3.anchor: or it is God Himself who answers the question (IK, Q, Ṭs).

TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r1.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r1.claim: Some Basran grammarians treat yawm as semantically annexed to the people in it, with an understood event such as their trial; this works when yawm means idh, but otherwise is awkward.
TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r1.anchor: فقال بعض نحويي البصرة: أضاف يوم إلى هم في المعنى، فلذلك لا ينون اليوم

TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r2.speaker: غيره
TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r2.claim: Another grammarian says time words function like idh and idhā, so they retain case forms; when a pronoun returns to them, they become full nouns and take tanwīn.
TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r2.anchor: وقال غيره: معنى ذلك: أن الأوقات جعلت بمعنى إذ وإذا، فلذلك بقيت على نصبها في الرفع والخفض والنصب

TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers treating yawm and similar time expressions as adverbial particles taking the case of their syntactic position; when they appear as nouns, they accept ordinary case inflection.
TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r3.anchor: والصواب من القول عندي في ذلك، أن نصب يوم وسائر الأزمنة في مثل هذا الموضع نظير نصب الأدوات لوقوعها مواقعها

TAB-FULL:v20p299/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p299/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p299/r1.claim: On the Resurrection Day, none of the people or any of their deeds from worldly life is hidden from God.
TAB-FULL:v20p299/r1.anchor: ولا من أعمالهم التي عملوها في الدنيا {شيء} [البقرة: 20]

TAB-FULL:v20p299/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p299/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p299/r2.claim: Qatāda says they emerge before God on Resurrection Day, unable to hide behind a mountain or a building of mud.
TAB-FULL:v20p299/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {يوم هم بارزون لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء} [غافر: 16] «ولكنهم برزوا له يوم القيامة، فلا يستترون بجبل ولا مدر»

TAB-FULL:v20p299#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p299#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p299#2/r1.claim: God answers His own question by declaring that sovereignty belongs to Him alone.
TAB-FULL:v20p299#2/r1.anchor: نفسه فيقول: {لله الواحد} [إبراهيم: 48] الذي لا مثل له ولا شبيه

TAB-FULL:v20p299#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p299#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p299#2/r2.claim: The question concerns authority on the Day of Resurrection; God has no equal and subdues everything by His power and might.
TAB-FULL:v20p299#2/r2.anchor: الذي لا مثل له ولا شبيه {القهار} [يوسف: 39] لكل شيء سواه بقدرته، الغالب بعزته

SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r1.claim: يوم may be appositive to يوم التلاق or governed by التلاق, meaning the meeting occurs on the day they appear.
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r1.anchor: أنه بدل من " يوم التلاق " بدل كل من كل. الثاني: أن ينتصب بالتلاق أي: يقع التلاقي في يوم بروزهم.

SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows يوم to be governed by لا يخفى on views that permit لا to govern a preceding word, except when it begins an oath's answer.
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r2.anchor: أن ينتصب بقوله: { لا يخفى على الله } ، ذكره ابن عطية، وهذا على أحد الأقوال الثلاثة في " لا "

SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r3.claim: A fourth parse makes يوم accusative under an implied اذكر.
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r3.anchor: الرابع: أن ينتصب بإضمار " اذكر ". و " يوم " ظرف مستقبل ك " إذا ".

SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r4.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r4.claim: Sibawayh rejects a future adverb annexed to a nominal clause and supplies an implied verb before the noun, unlike al-Akhfash.
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r4.anchor: وسيبوية لا يرى إضافة الظرف المستقبل إلى الجمل الاسمية، والأخفش يراه

SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r5.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash permits a future adverb to be annexed directly to a nominal clause.
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r5.anchor: والأخفش يراه، ولذلك قدر سيبويه في قوله:

SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r6.claim: Sibawayh's rule can be reconciled by taking هم as raised by an omitted verb explained by بارزون, with بارزون predicated of an omitted subject.
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r6.anchor: بأن " هم " ليس مبتدأ بل مرفوعا بفعل محذوف يفسره اسم الفاعل أي: يوم برزوا

SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r7.claim: يوم هم is generally treated as inflected; some permit building with a present verb or nominal clause, though some wrongly insist on building in the latter case.
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r7.anchor: وحركة " يوم هم " حركة إعراب على المشهور. ومنهم من جوز بناء الظرف، وإن أضيف إلى فعل مضارع أو جملة اسمية

SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r8.claim: Basrans build the adverb only when annexed to a past verb; here and in al-Dhariyat يوم هم is written separately, its original form.
SAMIN-DURR:40:16/r8.anchor: لا يبنى عند البصريين إلا ما أضيف إلى فعل ماض

SAMIN-DURR:40:16#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:16#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:16#2/r1.claim: لا يخفى may be independent, circumstantial of the pronoun in بارزون, or a second predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:40:16#2/r1.anchor: أن تكون مستأنفة، وأن تكون حالا

TABATABAI:40:16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:16/r1.claim: Meeting God means that distracting causes are cut off, God appears as manifest truth, and people are exposed to Him; the author links this wording to 32:10, 11:29, and 84:6.
TABATABAI:40:16/r1.anchor: ومعنى اللقاء تقطع الأسباب الشاغلة وظهور أن الله هو الحق المبين وبروزهم لله.

TABATABAI:40:16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:16/r2.claim: Their becoming manifest to God means imagined causes that drew them to themselves and veiled them from their Lord are removed, so they see His encompassing dominion and exclusive judgment, lordship, and divinity.
TABATABAI:40:16/r2.anchor: وارتفاع الأسباب الوهمية التي كانت تجذبهم إلى نفسها وتحجبهم عن ربهم وتغفلهم عن إحاطة ملكه وتفرده في الحكم وتوحده في الربوبية والالوهية.

TABATABAI:40:16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:16/r3.claim: “Nothing of them is hidden from God” explains their exposure: hearts, deeds, outward and inward states, and what they remembered or forgot are all uncovered.
TABATABAI:40:16/r3.anchor: فقلوبهم وأعمالهم بعين الله وظاهرهم وباطنهم وما ذكروه وما نسوه مكشوفة غير مستورة.

TABATABAI:40:16-20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:16-20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:16-20/r1.claim: The divine question and answer about ownership reveal the day's reality: God's dominion and authority over creation appear without restriction; His oneness and subduing power explain why ownership belongs only to Him.
TABATABAI:40:16-20/r1.anchor: سؤال وجواب من ناحيته سبحانه تبين بهما حقيقة اليوم وهي ظهور ملكه وسلطانه تعالى على الخلق على الإطلاق.

TABRISI:40:16/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:16/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:16/r2.claim: Today may be accusative as the time when sovereignty is established, or attached directly to sovereignty; some instead pause after sovereignty and begin today belongs to God.
TABRISI:40:16/r2.anchor: أي لمن ثبت الملك في هذا اليوم ويجوز أن يتعلق بنفس الملك

TABRISI:40:16-17/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:16-17/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:16-17/r16.claim: Those manifest emerge from their graves; alternatively, they become visible to one another as hidden states are disclosed.
TABRISI:40:16-17/r16.anchor: من قبورهم. وقيل: يبرز بعضهم لبعض فلا يخفى على أحد حال غيره

TABRISI:40:16-17/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:16-17/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:16-17/r17.claim: Nothing about their deeds or states is hidden from God.
TABRISI:40:16-17/r17.anchor: { لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء } أي من أعمالهم وأحوالهم

TABRISI:40:16-17/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:16-17/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:16-17/r18.claim: The creatures answer that sovereignty belongs to God alone; the author prefers this over God asking and answering Himself, since the verse describes servants emerging from graves.
TABRISI:40:16-17/r18.anchor: والأول أصح لأنه بين أنه يقول

TABRISI:40:16-17/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:16-17/r19.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TABRISI:40:16-17/r19.claim: God says and answers the sovereignty question between the two trumpet blasts, after all creation perishes and He alone remains.
TABRISI:40:16-17/r19.anchor: يقول الله تعالى ذلك بين النفختين حين يفني الخلائق كلها ثم يجيب نفسه لأنه بقي وحده

TABRISI:40:16-17/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:16-17/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:16-17/r20.claim: The Day is singled out because God had granted people some worldly control, while then no one owns anything; none merits unqualified kingship without being made owner by another.
TABRISI:40:16-17/r20.anchor: وإنما خص ذلك اليوم بأن له الملك فيه لأنه قد ملك العباد بعض الأمور في الدنيا ولا يملك أحد شيئا ذلك اليوم

TABRISI:40:16-17/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:16-17/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:16-17/r21.claim: An objection says prophets and believers have great dominion in the afterlife; the answer is that only God deserves the unqualified title King, or that the verse is before Paradise’s people receive their possessions.
TABRISI:40:16-17/r21.anchor: فإن قيل أليس يملك الأنبياء والمؤمنون في الآخرة الملك العظيم فالجواب: إن أحدا لا يستحق إطلاق الصفة بالملك إلا الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:14-16/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:14-16/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:14-16/r3.claim: On Resurrection Day people emerge from their graves and nothing of their deeds or wealth is hidden from God; He asks who owns sovereignty and answers: God, the One, the All-Prevailing.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:14-16/r3.anchor: يقول الله في ذلك اليوم: { لمن الملك اليوم } ثم يجيب نفسه { لله الواحد القهار }.

BAQILLANI:v1p198/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p198/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p198/r6.claim: The warning about the Day of Meeting leads into the scene where all are exposed, nothing is hidden from God, and the question of sovereignty is answered: it belongs to God, the One, the Subduer.
BAQILLANI:v1p198/r6.anchor: لينذر يوم التلاق يوم هم بارزون لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار

BAQILLANI:v1p199/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p199/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p199/r4.claim: This eloquence characterizes every verse, sūra, section, story, and meaning, though narrative, law, theology, proof, and instruction each call for a different kind of speech.
BAQILLANI:v1p199/r4.anchor: ولست أقول هذا لك في دون آية وسورة دون سورة وفصل دون فصل وقصة دون قصة ومعنى دون معنى

BAQILLANI:v1p199/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p199/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p199/r5.claim: Even accomplished writers vary by subject: a master poet falls short in ascetic verse, and a stylist writing legal rulings does not speak as he does on other topics.
BAQILLANI:v1p199/r5.anchor: إلا ترى أن الشاعر المفلق إذا جاء إلى الزهد قصر والأديب إذا تكلم في بيان الأحكام

BAQILLANI:v1p66/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p66/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p66/r1.claim: Bāqillānī asks whether Qur’anic inimitability can be recognized through badīʿ, the art of rhetorical embellishment, and introduces examples collected by its specialists.
BAQILLANI:v1p66/r1.anchor: إن سأل سائل فقال هل يمكن أن يعرف إعجاز القرآن من جهة ما تضمنه من البديع

BAQILLANI:v1p66/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p66/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p66/r5.claim: He calls expressions of divine majesty another kind of badīʿ, citing God’s possession of all things, the source of every blessing, and the proclamation that sovereignty belongs to the One, the Subduer.
BAQILLANI:v1p66/r5.anchor: وفي الألفاظ الإلهية كقوله ( ﴿ وله كل شيء ﴾ )

BAQILLANI:v1p66/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p66/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p66/r6.claim: He extends the catalogue to striking sayings of the Prophet, Abū Bakr, and ʿAlī, including compact advice, warnings, and memorable comparisons.
BAQILLANI:v1p66/r6.anchor: ويذكرون من البديع قول النبي خير الناس رجل ممسك بعنان فرسه في سبيل الله

BURHAN:v4p47/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p47/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p47/r7.claim: In ‘To whom belongs sovereignty today? To God,’ the answer omits the subject الملك; the full sense is ‘sovereignty belongs to God alone.’
BURHAN:v4p47/r7.anchor: إذ التقدير الملك لله الواحد فحذف المبتدأ من الجواب إذ المعنى لا ملك إلا لله

BURHAN:v1p418/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p418/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p418/r6.claim: يوم هم is separated because هم begins an independent sentence annexed to يوم; يومهم is joined because the possessive pronoun is part of the singular compound.
BURHAN:v1p418/r6.anchor: حرفان فصل الضمير منهما لأنه مبتدأ وأضيف اليوم إلى الجملة المنفصلة عنه

NASHR:v2p149/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p149/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p149/r6.claim: The phrase yawm hum is written separately in its two listed occurrences.
NASHR:v2p149/r6.anchor: (ويوم هم) مفصول في موضعين يوم هم بارزون في غافر ويوم هم على النار في الذاريات
